candidates.label: B056-reorder (control/defense fix, not a general fix)
candidates.change: A and B phoenix_init: 'mov bx,imm; push cs; pop ss' -> 'push cs; mov bx,imm; pop ss' (zero bytes, same turn count, identical machine state afterwards). Removes the 4-byte initializer signature 0E 17 89 07 (A offset 43h, B offset 8Fh). Sources agent2/night/scratch/B056/fixA.asm, fixB.asm.

threatFindings.threat: Original New_Best (INT87 search 0E 17 BB 00 -> FF 26 17 4A, the m048-killer) against rev0
threatFindings.evidence: rev0 A/B contain no 0E 17 BB 00 (V6 lineage already uses the hardened order 16 1F BB C0/80 02 0E 17). Threat i8i0e NB_orig cohorts: base and reorder candidate produce identical battles (diff exactly 0); base team 0.346/battle there, New_Best team 0.585 (it is a strong same-lineage opponent, not a signature killer of rev0).
threatFindings.impact: none via signature; New_Best is still a strong lattice peer

threatFindings.threat: New_Best-style 4-byte INT87 search-and-replace retargeted at a late-executed rev0 initializer string: 0E 17 89 07 = push cs; pop ss; mov [bx],ax (A offset 43h executed ~turn 39-41; B offset 8Fh executed ~turn 41-43; counter's INT87 runs at its instruction 10-12, std from DI=0, two charges hit A and B)
threatFindings.evidence: Threat i8i0e (480 battles/arm, 8 cohorts per threat, base rev0): vs NB_sig0E178907 (New_Best with DX imm 00BBh->0789h, replacement FF 26 17 4A jmp [4A17h]) base team 0.0000/battle (A 0.000, B 0.000 over 160 battles); vs NB_sigkill (same search, replacement CC CC CC CC) base 0.052. Reorder candidate scores 0.342 / 0.373 in the same cohorts (diff +0.342 [0.294,0.389] and +0.321 [0.252,0.390], 8/0 each). Counter team score 0.654 vs base, 0.512 vs candidate. The jmp [4A17h] capture also kills because New_Best2 wins the [4A17h] write race (its instr 4 vs rev0 B instr 3) and the hijacked process runs with DS=private, copying a garbage worker.
threatFindings.impact: -0.34 points/battle per cohort containing such a counter; total wipe-out of both warriors

threatFindings.threat: Generality: any late-executed initializer 4-byte string is exploitable; signature reorders only move the hole
threatFindings.evidence: Threat x4a43: counter retargeted to 17 89 07 83 (pop ss; mov [bx],ax; and dx,..; A offset 44h, B offset 90h, present in both rev0 and the reorder fix): base 0.0063 and fix 0.0063 (diff exactly 0, 160 battles), counter team 0.6875.
threatFindings.impact: no zero-cost general fix exists; a defense only works against a known published signature (m049-style reorder)

threatFindings.threat: Realistic exposure: does any published 2025/2024 opponent or reference pair search a 4-byte string present in rev0 A/B?
threatFindings.evidence: Static scan agent2/night/scratch/B056/scan.mjs of all INT87 call sites (immediate AX/DX) in official-2025 senior+young, cgx2024 03-live and 05-final2, 2025 zombies, refs V6/V4/V6Guard/zchain4, New_Best: no signature matches any 4-byte window of rev0 A or B. Screen fqpr7: the reorder that changes 7 initializer windows gives bit-identical results on all 1500 field-S battles. Caveat: a few INT87 sites compute AX/DX (ADDvanced, almogooners, OtoGlida, HLS_segment_fault) and are not resolved statically, but they had zero effect in field S cohorts where present.
threatFindings.impact: ~0 in the archived fields; risk only from a purpose-built counter that copies V6 bytes (V6 code is circulating)

threatFindings.threat: Anchor searchers FF 1F CC CC (OpcodeHunter1, 2B2Team, PastRAMa, ATO1, JMP2HELL2, segment_fault) matching the dwell-phase anchor FF 1F followed by untouched CC CC
threatFindings.evidence: Static only: the pattern matches each generation's anchor during dwell, but these searchers fire at their startup (instr ~10-30) before our first anchor exists (~turn 52); not tested here (anchor domain, not initializer).

counterCodes.strength: total kill of rev0: base 0.000/battle, counter 0.654 (threat i8i0e)
hits rev0 AND the reorder fix: both 0.0063/battle, counter 0.6875 (threat x4a43)
original New_Best (db form, hashes 81ca1a63/4480aef2): no signature effect on rev0

recommendation: Do not promote the reorder (screen exactly 0; it only defeats one specific counter and a 1-word retarget defeats it again). Classify domain 6 as: mechanism verified-in-current and catastrophic against a purpose-built counter, but not present in any archived field. A general defense would require removing late-executed unique initializer strings or racing/decoying searches; worth considering only if a V6-targeting signature counter is expected in the 2026 field. Counters nbsigA/B and nbsig2A/B are ready test cases for R3/R4/R5 roles.
